nodes.description: Cells expressing R704C collagen II show no splicing of XBP-1 and no activated caspase-3, meaning neither the unfolded protein response nor apoptosis is engaged. This is the mechanistic point on which the disorder separates from both the C-terminal COL2A1 dysplasias and the COMP- and MATN3-related forms of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia, in all of which mutant cartilage protein is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum and the resulting stress response is the proximate cause of chondrocyte dysfunction.

nodes.description: Type II collagen is a homotrimer of three alpha-1(II) chains, so in a heterozygote roughly seven of every eight molecules incorporate at least one mutant chain. Recombinant R704C collagen II is trypsin-resistant, gives a normal collagen circular-dichroism spectrum, and is recovered mainly from the culture supernatant, so the mutant chain reaches the extracellular space carrying an unpaired cysteine that the wild-type sequence does not have.
